title: Cap. 7 Patrum: Fulgentius — special will and predestination in Christ
pass_a_gloss: 6. Fulgentius, On the Incarnation and grace of Jesus Christ, chapter 29, page 92, Library of the Fathers, volume 6. Those who think the will of God by which he wills all human beings to be saved is equal concerning the redeemed and the damned — when they have been asked why God wills all human beings to be saved and yet not all are saved — what will they answer? The most learned Fulgentius hints that God by a special will decreed that the salvation of those who are in fact saved should be procured through Christ; and that those who affirm the contrary have nothing solid to answer when they are pressed to show whence this difference arises, that some are actually saved by Christ's death and others are not saved. He demonstrates that this cannot be referred to a difference of human wills — chapters 30 and 31. 7. I add another testimony of the same Fulgentius, book 3 On the truth of Predestination. Those whom God predestined to the adoption of sons — that no Christian ought to doubt they were predestined in Christ before the foundation of the world not only to the reward of glorification but to the grace of justification, and by the benefit of this predestination called and justified according to purpose. Whoever does not doubt that the elect sons of God were predestined in Christ both to grace and to glory before the world's foundation will freely confess that Christ's death and merit were ordained and accepted in a certain special manner for those same elect, so that from thence they might infallibly obtain this grace and glory destined for them.
pass_b_english: 6. Fulgentius, On the Incarnation and grace of Jesus Christ 29 (Bibliotheca Patrum, vol. 6, p. 92): Those who treat God's will that all be saved as the same toward the redeemed and the damned — when asked why God wills all to be saved and yet not all are — what answer have they? Fulgentius implies that God by a special will decreed to procure, through Christ, the salvation of those who are in fact saved; and that their opponents have nothing solid left when pressed to explain why some are actually saved by Christ's death and others are not. He shows this difference cannot be reduced to a difference of human wills (chs. 30-31). 7. Another from the same Fulgentius, On the truth of Predestination, book 3: No Christian should doubt that those God predestined to the adoption of sons were predestined in Christ before the world's foundation not only to the reward of glory but to the grace of justification, and by that predestination's benefit called and justified according to purpose. Anyone who grants that God's elect sons were so predestined in Christ to grace and glory will freely admit that Christ's death and merit were ordained and accepted in a special way for those same elect, so that from them they might obtain without fail the grace and glory marked out for them.
source_text: 6. Fulgentius, De Incarn. & grat. Jesu Chr. cap. 29. p. 92. Biblioth. Patr. tom. 6. Hi qui voluntatem Dei, qua omnes homines vult salvos fieri, aequalem circa redimendos & damnandos existimant, cum interrogati fuerint cur Deus velit omnes homines salvos fieri, nec tamen omnes salvi fiant, quid respondebunt? Innuit doctissimus Fulgentius, Deum speciali voluntate illorum salutem per Christum procurandam decrevisse qui de facto salvantur; eosque qui contrarium affirmant, nihil solidi habere quod respondeant, quando urgentur ut ostendant, unde hoc discrimen oriatur, quod quidam morte Christi reapse salvantur, alii non salvantur. Ad humanarum voluntatum discrimen hoc revocari non posse demonstrat. cap. 30. & 31. 7. Adjungo aliud testimonium ejusdem Fulgentii, lib. 3. De verit. Praedest. Quos Deus praedestinavit in adoptionem Filiorum, hos non solum ad praemium glorificationis sed ad gratiam justificationis ante mundi constitutionem in Christo praedestinatos, & hujus praedestinationis beneficio secundum propositum vocatos & justificatos, nullus debet ambigere Christianus. Qui non ambigit electos Dei filios fuisse in Christo tam ad gratiam, quam ad gloriam ante mundi constitutionem praedestinatos, ille ultro fatebitur, mortem meritumque Christi fuisse speciali quadam ratione pro eisdem electis ordinatum & acceptatum, ut inde possent hanc gratiam & gloriam sibi destinatam infallibiliter obtinere.
